payload.hypothesis: Replacing pointwise logloss with a within-user listwise softmax (cross-entropy over each user's impression group, positives as the target distribution) raises validation primary by more than 0.002 over the 0.60147 pointwise FM.
payload.mechanism: The metric is fully determined by within-user ordering. Pointwise BCE spends model capacity on calibrating the absolute rate per row (including per-user base rates, which C2/C23 prove are metric no-ops), and weights every row equally regardless of its group. A softmax over one user's impressions produces gradients that depend only on score differences inside the group, which is exactly the quantity GAUC and nDCG@5 read. This should sharpen the ordering of mixed-label users -- the only users GAUC scores at all -- without needing more features or capacity.

payload.hypothesis: Adding a within-user listwise softmax term ON TOP OF the pointwise logloss (weight lambda, applied only to mixed-label groups, after a pointwise warm-up) raises validation primary above 0.60147 by at least +0.002, whereas replacing the pointwise loss entirely (iter 1) lowered it.
payload.mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 both depend only on the ordering of scores inside one user's impression list. Pointwise BCE spends capacity matching the global positive rate (~0.33) and pays no penalty for a constant within-user offset error; the softmax term penalises exactly the within-user score differences the metric reads, and its gradient (softmax(s) - normalised label) directly pushes a user's positives above that user's negatives. Keeping the BCE anchor preserves the well-conditioned per-row signal that made the pure listwise run under-fit, while restricting the listwise term to mixed-label groups removes ~42% of groups whose softmax target carries no ordering information.

payload.hypothesis: Adding smoothed, strictly-prior user-conditioned preference rates over item attributes (user x dur_bucket, user x tab) as bucketized FM fields raises validation primary by more than 0.002, because these are dense explicit estimates of exactly the user-item crosses the low-rank FM cannot learn (98.4% of validation user-video pairs are novel).
payload.mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 only see within-user ordering. A user's smoothed prior long_view rate for the duration band / tab of the candidate is a quantity that differs across that user's own impressions, so it directly reorders the list. The FM currently has to express 'this user likes long videos' as a user_id x dur_bucket embedding dot product estimated from that user's ~35 train rows spread over all fields; an explicit smoothed rate is a far lower-variance estimator of the same quantity, and its first-order weight alone already produces a within-user reordering.
payload.predicted: +0.003 to +0.006 valid primary (0.6045-0.6075); a null result would be < +0.001
payload.invalid_if: Validation primary comes in at or below 0.6035 (delta <= +0.002), or the encoded validation distribution of the new fields is degenerate (>80% of validation rows in the zero-count bin, or the rate field near-constant within users).
evidence: C12: 98.114% of validation users and 99.882% of videos are warm, but only 1.627% of user-video pairs and 3.376% of user-author pairs were ever seen in train -- the FM must reach every personalized cross through 16-dim embeddings.

C2 / README: pure user-side first-order terms score exactly zero; user information can only act through terms that vary within the user's list. user x dur_bucket varies within essentially every validation list (median 4 impressions, mixed durations).

C15: removing `tab` costs -0.0159 primary, ~8x epsilon, so tab-conditioned behaviour is where the largest single measured signal in this model lives; a per-user tab rate is the personalized version of that signal.
C13: 98.114% of validation users have >=1 prior train interaction, median 35 / mean 47 prior rows, so cell counts for a 8-15 valued item attribute are non-trivial for most users.
Organizer headroom idea 2 (behavioural history) has never been attempted in this run; iters 1-2 spent on objective changes only.
harness.history.prior_stats supports tuple keys and Bayesian smoothing with strictly-earlier-only, ties-excluded guarantees proven by tests.
payload.reason: The hypothesis predicted +0.003 to +0.006; the measured delta is -0.0013, which is more than 2 sigma below zero and clearly fails the invalid_if threshold (<=+0.002). This is not a null result, it's a mild regression: adding the three history fields made the FM worse, not better.
payload.mechanism_update: The claim that an explicit smoothed prior rate is automatically a lower-variance, easier-to-use signal than what the FM's embeddings already approximate does not hold in practice. Likely causes: (1) bucketizing the rate into 7 quantile bins plus a reserved zero-history bin adds three new categorical fields the FM must fit fresh embeddings for, diluting capacity and introducing noise from the discretization itself; (2) the user x tab cross was substituted for the hypothesized user x dur_bucket cross, so the feature may not target the interaction the FM actually struggles with; (3) count_tab regularly hits the count<=0 reserved bucket, and tab-level history per user is sparse enough that these bucketized rates carry limited signal while adding vocabulary/parameter overhead. Net effect: added fields cost more (extra sparse embeddings, encoding noise) than they contribute in reordering signal.
deprioritise: user x tab smoothed-rate bucketized features
naive substitution of tab for dur_bucket in history crosses
quantile-bucketized prior-rate fields as categorical FM inputs without validating bucket occupancy first
